# Guided AI GRC Build: Proposal for Tamarack Instruments

**Prepared for:** Dana Whitfield, General Counsel
**Program:** Guided AI GRC Build, twelve weeks, US$60,000

## 1. Situation Summary

Tamarack Instruments designs and manufactures laboratory measurement instruments. It has about 1,100 staff, is headquartered in the Netherlands and operates in the Netherlands, Germany and the United States. The EU AI Act and GDPR are its stated regulatory drivers.

The Client's AI use spans three stages:

- **Deployed:** a customer service chatbot on the support portal.
- **Piloting:** AI visual inspection on the German production line.
- **Planned:** AI sales forecasting next year.

An internal audit finding in June 2026 recorded that there is no inventory of AI systems. The Client operates an ISO/IEC 27001 ISMS, an ISO 9001 quality management system and an internal audit function. It intends to pursue ISO/IEC 42001, with work to start next year and the start date not yet fixed.

The stated objective, in Dana Whitfield's words, is: "I want governance in place before visual inspection goes into production in Q2 2027."

Three constraints apply:

- Budget is approved up to US$80,000 this fiscal year.
- Customer data must stay in the EU.
- The German works council is consulted before anything touches production staff.

## 2. Why a Guided Build Rather Than Consulting Delivery

A consulting engagement would hand Tamarack Instruments a finished set of documents. A guided build hands over a working system and a team that knows how to run it.

In the Guided AI GRC Build, the Client's own build team produces every artifact during structured asynchronous work between sessions. A weekly workshop teaches the method and a weekly coaching session tests the work. At Week 12, the people who will operate the AI Management System (AIMS) are the people who built it. They understand why each control exists and can maintain it without outside dependency.

This matters for Tamarack Instruments for three reasons:

1. **It works within systems the Client already runs.** The build attaches to the existing ISMS and quality management system rather than standing up a parallel structure.
2. **It builds operating evidence.** By Week 12 the system has been running and producing records, which is what later ISO/IEC 42001 readiness work will need to show.
3. **It applies three principles throughout:** Slow AI, Informed Intent, Final Liability rests with the Human.

The program draws on two open frameworks:

- GRC Workbook (https://github.com/rolldabones/grc-workbook) provides the governance artifacts.
- Slow AI Kitchen (https://github.com/rolldabones/slow-ai-kitchen) provides the governed workflow method.

AI Governance for Boards (https://github.com/rolldabones/ai-governance-for-boards) serves as the reference for board-layer reporting at the steering checkpoints.

## 3. The Twelve-Week Spine, Tailored to Tamarack Instruments

**Inventory order.** Systems enter the Week 2 inventory in this order:

1. **The customer service chatbot** goes first because it is deployed.
2. **AI visual inspection** goes second because it is piloting and the stated objective ties governance to its move to production in Q2 2027.
3. **AI sales forecasting** is recorded third as a planned system, so it enters governance before it is built.

Week 2 also includes a discovery exercise to identify any further AI systems in use. The full population is Unknown.

**Mapping to ISO/IEC 42001.** The readiness theme column shows where each artifact supports later ISO/IEC 42001 work. It indicates readiness only and implies no certification or audit outcome.

| Week | Focus and Tailoring | Key Artifact | ISO/IEC 42001 Readiness Theme |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Mobilization, charter and roles; first steering checkpoint | Draft AIMS charter, RACI | Context, leadership and roles (Clauses 4, 5) |
| 2 | AI system inventory, starting with chatbot, visual inspection and forecasting | Populated inventory | Context and scope (Clause 4); resources (Annex A.4) |
| 3 | Classification and risk methodology, including EU AI Act classification of each inventoried system | Classification record, risk criteria | Planning and risk criteria (Clause 6.1) |
| 4 | Risk and impact assessments for chatbot and visual inspection; GDPR touchpoints identified | Assessments for both systems | AI risk assessment and AI system impact assessment (Clauses 6.1.2, 6.1.4; Annex A.5) |
| 5 | Risk register and treatment | Operating risk register | Risk treatment (Clause 6.1.3) |
| 6 | Policy set; mid-point steering | Core policy set for adoption | AI policy (Clause 5.2; Annex A.2) |
| 7 | Operating procedures and lifecycle governance | Lifecycle procedures | Operation (Clause 8; Annex A.6) |
| 8 | Vendor and supplier governance; evidence collection starts | Supplier assessments, evidence tracker | Third-party relationships (Annex A.10); documented information (Clause 7.5) |
| 9 | Governed workflows and human oversight using Slow AI Kitchen | At least two governed workflows | Use of AI systems and human oversight (Annex A.9) |
| 10 | Testing, evaluation and monitoring, including visual inspection performance monitoring | Monitoring plan and first results | Monitoring and measurement (Clause 9.1) |
| 11 | Incident response, change management and evidence review | Incident and change procedures | Nonconformity and improvement (Clause 10) |
| 12 | Audit readiness review, evidence walkthrough and closing steering | Readiness review, closing report | Internal audit and management review readiness (Clauses 9.2, 9.3) |

**Integration with incumbent frameworks.**

- **ISO/IEC 27001 ISMS:** integration point Unknown, to confirm at intake.
- **ISO 9001 quality management system:** integration point Unknown, to confirm at intake.
- **Internal audit function:** the June 2026 finding is the stated artifact. The Week 2 inventory and the Week 11 and Week 12 evidence reviews are the points where the build responds to it. Whether the finding is addressed is for internal audit to determine.

**Legal-effect items.** EU AI Act classification, GDPR assessment, customer data residency, works council consultation, charter adoption and policy adoption all have legal effect. Confirm with external counsel.

## 4. Contracted Outcome: Minimum Viable AIMS at Week 12

The contracted outcome is a minimum viable AIMS comprising:

1. An adopted charter.
2. A populated inventory.
3. An operating risk register.
4. An adopted core policy set.
5. At least two governed AI workflows in production use.
6. Evidence collection running for at least four weeks.

**Dependency on the second governed workflow.** The chatbot is deployed. Visual inspection is piloting and is targeted for production in Q2 2027. AI sales forecasting is planned for next year. Which second workflow will be in production use by Week 12 therefore needs to be settled at intake. If that workflow touches production staff, the German works council consultation must be scheduled so that it is complete before Week 9. Confirm with external counsel.

**Questions to confirm at intake:**

- Does the chatbot process customer data, and where is it hosted relative to the EU data residency constraint?
- Are the chatbot and the visual inspection system vendor-supplied?
- Which ISMS and quality management system artifacts exist for the build to attach to?
- Who is the internal build lead?
- How will the two internal auditors take part while preserving audit independence? We propose they act as assurance advisers to the build rather than artifact owners.

## 5. Client Team Commitment

The table below gives estimated hours per week by role, including the workshop and coaching session. Effort actuals are Unknown and will be tracked from Week 1.

| Role | Estimated Hours per Week | Estimated Peak Weeks |
|---|---|---|
| General Counsel | 3 to 4 (estimate) | W1, W3, W6, W12 |
| CISO | 3 to 4 (estimate) | W4, W8, W11 |
| Head of Quality | 4 to 5 (estimate) | W7, W10, W11 |
| Head of Data | 4 to 6 (estimate) | W2, W4, W10 |
| German plant manager | 2 to 3 (estimate) | W2, W4, W9, W10 |
| Internal auditor (each of two) | 2 to 3 (estimate) | W2, W11, W12 |
| Internal build lead (Unknown) | 6 to 8 (estimate) | All weeks |

## 6. Steering Cadence

Executive steering checkpoints take place at Weeks 1, 6 and 12:

- **Week 1:** approves scope, team and the second-workflow plan.
- **Week 6:** reviews spine status, blockers and scope decisions.
- **Week 12:** receives the minimum viable AIMS attestation, an evidence sample index and a 12-month operating plan.

Board-layer reporting follows AI Governance for Boards (https://github.com/rolldabones/ai-governance-for-boards). We propose that Dana Whitfield chairs steering. Other attendees are to be confirmed at intake.

## 7. Logistics and Price

- **Format:** one live virtual workshop, one coaching session and structured asynchronous implementation each week for twelve weeks.
- **Price:** US$60,000. This sits within the stated budget approval of up to US$80,000 this fiscal year. The fiscal year dates are Unknown and should be confirmed against the start date.
- **Start date:** Unknown. For illustration, a start in the first week of January 2027 would close in late March 2027, ahead of Q2 2027. Any later start moves the close date accordingly.
- **Session times and working language:** to confirm at intake.
- **Payment terms and contract:** to be agreed. Confirm with external counsel.

## 8. Next Step

A decision is expected by 15 December 2026. We propose a 60-minute intake call before that date to resolve the questions in Section 4, confirm the start date and agree the steering membership.
